title: "Prolog — Core Concepts"

# Prolog — describe relations, then ask questions

Prolog is not a sequence of assignments. We state **facts and rules** and ask whether a relation can be proved. Its engine uses unification and backtracking to search for solutions.

## 1. Facts represent relations

~~~prolog
parent(ann, bob).
parent(bob, cat).
~~~

The fact parent(ann,bob) says Ann is Bob's parent. It is not a function that returns a value.

Ask a query:

~~~prolog
?- parent(ann, bob).
true.
~~~

## 2. Variables unify with values

~~~prolog
?- parent(ann, Child).
Child = bob.
~~~

A capitalised name such as Child is a variable. The engine finds a binding that makes the query match a fact.

## 3. Rules express new relationships

~~~prolog
grandparent(X, Z) :- parent(X, Y), parent(Y, Z).
~~~

Read the rule as: X is a grandparent of Z if there exists a Y who is a child of X and parent of Z.

$$
G(x,z)\iff\exists y:\ P(x,y)\land P(y,z)
$$

**Symbols:** G(x,z) is the grandparent relation; P(x,y) is the parent relation; there exists means at least one intermediary y; and the symbol AND requires both parent relations.

**Concrete substitution:** With parent(ann,bob) and parent(bob,cat), choose x=ann, y=bob, z=cat. Both required facts are true, so grandparent(ann,cat) holds.

## 4. Backtracking finds alternatives

~~~prolog
color(red).
color(blue).
~~~

Querying color(X) produces X=red and, when you request another answer, X=blue. This is search over possible matching facts, not an imperative for-loop.

## 5. Recursion needs a base case

~~~prolog
ancestor(X, Y) :- parent(X, Y).
ancestor(X, Z) :- parent(X, Y), ancestor(Y, Z).
~~~

The base case is a direct parent; the recursive case follows one parent link then continues searching. For parent(ann,bob), parent(bob,cat), the query ancestor(ann,cat) succeeds.

**Important limitation:** Prolog's default depth-first search can loop on cyclic or poorly ordered recursive rules even when a logical answer exists. Logical meaning and operational search behaviour are related but not identical.

## 6. A small complete file

Put the facts plus grandparent and ancestor rules into family.pl. Run SWI-Prolog and query grandparent(ann,cat). One file is enough; no agent framework is needed.

**Official source:** [SWI-Prolog manual](https://www.swi-prolog.org/pldoc/man?section=quickstart), [The Art of Prolog reference](https://www.swi-prolog.org/pldoc/).
